chunks: Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Abū al-ʿAbbās, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was brought a short, ugly man whose belly was swollen and whose abdominal veins had become prominent; he had committed illicit intercourse with a woman. The woman said, “I knew nothing except that he had entered upon me.” So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said to him, “Did you commit zina?” He said, “Yes,” and he was not muḥṣan. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله raised his gaze and lowered it, then called for a palm cluster, counted it as one hundred stalks, and then struck him with its stalks.

key_terms.بِعِذْقٍ: with a palm cluster or branch
key_terms.زَنَيْتَ: committed zina, meaning illicit sexual intercourse
key_terms.شِمْرَاخٍ: a stalk or strand of a date-palm cluster
key_terms.مُحْصَنًا: legally protected through marriage, i.e. one in the status of iḥṣān

ai.seo_question: How was the hadd punishment for zina applied to a non-muḥṣan offender in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a case brought before the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله involving a man who confessed to zina while not being muḥṣan. It describes the implementation of the prescribed corporal punishment using a palm cluster containing one hundred stalks, reflecting a juridical ruling related to the hadd of zina.
